The definitions of n,u,T and the candidate Maxwellian assert no converse characterization of densities. The velocity domain is R^3 and periods L_j are positive; the zero density is handled separately by leaving u,T undefined. The construction has exactly three velocity coordinates, not a varying number of species or members. The kinetic fields are defined sectionwise on an open I; no time trace or time limiting operation is asserted. Carrier unchanged; owning contract review metadata only.

Current assigned boundary review: The symmetric measure and declared operator domain are supplied model data, not an equivalence theorem. Membership of polynomial or logarithmic tests in S_f is an additional requirement, not a converse deduction from weak identities. All collision tests are at a fixed velocity-density section on Q_el; no temporal endpoint appears in this definition. Carrier unchanged; owning contract review metadata only.

Current assigned boundary review: The proposed zero-production implication is refuted by the origin Dirac measure and a non-Gaussian positive density; no iff is asserted. The varying Hessian of log f disproves Maxwellian form; the example asserts no reverse characterization of restricted-support measures. The stationary velocity witness uses no time variable, only Gaussian decay at velocity infinity. The measure delta_(0,0,0,0), the zero operator, the span of the listed tests and the sinusoidal density are explicitly prescribed. Carrier unchanged; owning contract review metadata only.

Current assigned boundary review: Checked all three counterexample steps and exact local kinematic/exponential suppliers: R=exp(t Omega) is orthogonal with det 1; chi induces Omega x; Q=R(-t) gives u*=0, contrary to required mu Omega. Positive mu and nonzero skew Omega are essential. No measured data or admissibility claim enters. External reading covers MIT section 2.2 printed pp.33-34 and Tong sections 3.1-3.1.1 printed pp.58-61; the MIT section1.1 reference is only contextual and the explicit local suppliers prove the identities. Carrier unchanged; owning contract review metadata only.

Current assigned boundary review: The false assertion is a one-way implication from weak H convergence to weak L1 tensor convergence, refuted by sin(2 pi n x1/L)e2. No implication from tensor convergence back to velocity convergence is claimed; the constant (2,2) matrix test already refutes the stated implication. d>=2 and L>0 give the normalized nonempty torus; the witness is an infinite positive-integer frequency sequence. The witness needs the second coordinate and d>=2; a single sequence term does not assert a one-member convergence result. The length L=0 and dimension d=1 are excluded; the weak limit zero is retained and tensors have nonzero constant mean. The Fourier sequence has no time parameter or time trace; its limiting operation is n tending to infinity. The sine fields and constant matrix test are explicit. Countable Choice remains an inherited hypothesis of Fourier density, not an arbitrary-family selector. Carrier unchanged; owning contract review metadata only.

Current assigned boundary review: H and V are defined as closures of D_sigma; only passage of divergence to a given H1 limit is proved. The Definition expressly withholds the converse density characterization of all divergence-free H0^1 fields on arbitrary open Omega. Omega is explicitly a nonempty bounded open subset of R^3, so no empty-region closure theorem is claimed. The three spatial coordinates are fixed; no cardinality or dimension-one parameter is varied. The zero vector lies in both linear closures, but no collapse of the nonempty open spatial region is allowed. The H and V closures are spatial Sobolev constructions with no time variable. Carrier unchanged; owning contract review metadata only.

Current assigned boundary review: Positive n,T,m,k_B yield the five displayed Gaussian moment identities through rescaling, oddness and integration by parts; no characterization is claimed. All integrals are over fixed R^3 and n,T>0; there is no empty velocity family. The Gaussian has three coordinates and scalar normalization n; no one-dimensional parameter family is quantified. These are velocity integrals at fixed parameters. Vanishing Gaussian boundary terms at infinity are justified, and no temporal trace is asserted. Carrier unchanged; owning contract review metadata only.
